item.title: Native Beat: Native American Music of Sonoma County — Sat Nov 21, 2:00 PM — Sonoma Valley Library
item.description:
Professor Paul Steward presents a lecture and performance of Native American music from local tribal cultures, and a selection of different tribal cultures across the USA. Paul Steward is an accomplished educator, professional musician, and enrolled tribal member of the Elem Indian Colony of Pomo Indians. Serving as a Lecturer in Native American and American Indian Studies at San Francisco State University and Sonoma State University since 2016, he specializes in California Indian history, culture, and tribal relations. Parallel to his academic career, Steward is a celebrated singer, songwriter, and guitarist with over 20 years of professional experience. By uniquely blending traditional Pomo rhythms, language, and instruments with modern blues and soul, his work creates a vital cultural bridge that has earned him prestigious accolades, including the Native American Music Awards and recognition as a Yerba Buena Center for the Arts honoree.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

The Sunday before Thanksgiving, give yourself somewhere steady to stand.
Who it’s for: All levels. No advanced experience needed, just curiosity and a sense of play.
The holidays have a way of pulling us off center. Travel, family, full calendars, and everyone wanting a piece of you. This workshop is ninety minutes to find your footing first, in your body and in your head, before the season sweeps you up.

item.title: Santa's Reading Corner at the Meritage — Sun Nov 22, 2:00 PM — The Meritage Resort and Spa
item.description:
Experience the wonder of the season as Santa Claus himself makes The Meritage his home for the holidays. Watch your little one's eyes sparkle with delight as they meet Santa strolling through our festive village, a prelude to an enchanting afternoon. As the clock nears half-past three, gather in a cozy corner as Santa settles in to read a classic holiday tale. This cherished tradition takes place every weekend from Thanksgiving to Christmas, inviting your family to create treasured memories that will last a lifetime.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Wine Tasting Party for Singles 40+ at Bienvenue — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — 834 McClelland Drive
item.description:
The Wine Tasting Party for Singles 40+ at Bienvenue Vineyards Wine Lounge offers an opportunity for single wine lovers to mingle and make new connections in a relaxed setting. Guests can enjoy three complimentary wine tastings, participate in a fun mixer game, and bring a friend at no additional cost. Hosted by the Society of Single Professionals and SinglesBayArea, the event also supports the Seva Foundation, which works to restore sight to people experiencing blindness. Free street parking is available, and the SMART train provides convenient access.
Source: Sonoma.com

item.title: The Grateful Gathering at Sebastopol Center — Sun Nov 22, 4:30 PM — 282 S. High Street
item.description:
The Grateful Gathering: A Thanksgiving Celebration of The Grateful Dead brings a festive evening of live music honoring the Grateful Dead, Jerry Garcia and beyond. Led by Marcus Rezak, leader of the Grateful Dead tribute project Shred Is Dead, the performance features an accomplished lineup of musicians with connections to Umphrey’s McGee, Trey Anastasio Band, Phil Lesh and other notable artists. A graduate of Berklee and DePaul, Rezak is known for his improvisational style and high-energy performances. The celebration also features Anna Elva, Steve Pile, Stephanie Salva, Steven Younger, Sam Betty and Matt Petruska. The event serves as a fundraiser for Sebastopol Center for the Arts.
Source: Sonoma.com, North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Sebastopol Calendar, Visit Santa Rosa

item.title: Petaluma Holiday Food Fair at Hall of the Above — Mon Nov 23, 3:00 PM — 199 Petaluma Blvd North
item.description:
The 10th Annual Petaluma Holiday Food Fair brings dozens of local food makers together under one roof for an afternoon of holiday shopping and tasting. Visitors can browse a variety of locally made products, including cheese, bread, charcuterie, chocolate, honey, preserves, wine, and spirits, with the opportunity to shop directly from the makers. For the first time, the annual event takes place at Barber Lee Spirits Distillery in downtown Petaluma, where guests can also sample the distillery’s spirits and enjoy seasonal cocktails and other beverages amid festive holiday decorations. Free tickets are required, with reservations offered in 15-minute entry intervals to help manage attendance. Children do not need tickets.
Source: Sonoma.com

item.title: Discovering Women Poets, a Poetry Competition — Thu Nov 26, 9:00 AM — https://www.goldengatemarinart.org/
item.description:
The National League of American Pen Women (NLAPW) and the Golden Gate-Marin Branch are launching a poetry competition for women over 18 years of age who are not currently members of the NLAPW. This regional and national competition will be run at the Branch level in the semi-finalist phase. Local winners are automatically entered into the League’s National competition.
Winners at the Branch level will receive $35 and have their entry published in the Branch newsletter. They will also be invited to present their poetry in person or by Zoom.
Branch winners become semi-finalists in the National competition, which will award $100 to three winners. National winners will have their work and a short bio published in The Pen Woman, a national magazine. All semi-finalists will be listed in the magazine.

item.title: No Venom Cocktail Tasting at The Porch — Fri Nov 27, 3:30 PM — MacArthur Place
item.description:
Join Sonoma locals Adrienne and Tito, founders of No Venom, for a spirited tasting experience at The Porch. Discover five thoughtfully crafted non-alcoholic cocktails, including the Vesper, Fer-de-Lance, Sidewinder, Black Mamba, and Blue Racer, as they share the ingredients and inspiration behind each creation. Enjoy them alcohol-free or add a little "venom" with Lighthouse Gin or Higher Ground Vodka, and discover how these locally inspired cocktails have found a home on the menu at Layla.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: 2026 ACORN MUSH BLUES FESTIVAL — Fri Nov 27, 7:00 PM — Soper Reese Theatre
item.description:
American blues and roots music is treasured by all, and certainly in the Native American community as well. The Acorn Mush Blues Festival highlights local native musicians and artists who over the years crafted their own style of that music. Just as acorns are gathered and processed into a fine delicious meal, so is the music. Weaving Blues, country, rock, pop, Jazz, and R&B with our traditional native music.
Pomo Cultural series - Presented by the Lake County Arts Council
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Saturday Harvest Market at Sonoma Garden Park — Sat Nov 28, 9:00 AM — Sonoma Garden Park
item.description:
Sonoma Garden Park’s 2023 full Harvest Markets are on Saturdays, 9:00 am-12:00 pm, starting from April 22, 2023. The Harvest Market is a great place to pick up produce, flowers, and eggs harvested from our 6.1 acre sustainable garden. We will be selling products such as fresh produce, eggs from free-range chickens, honey, and olive oil. The market now accepts credit cards. Remember to bring your reusable shopping bag!
To stay updated on our events, sign up for our newsletter at: sonomaecologycenter.org/newsletters-sign-up
